page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.large is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at 3.4 GHz, built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 2 physical cores, 1 thread per core, and 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, but small-block cached read bandwidth and overall PassMark memory scores are weak. Database operations and static web serving throughput also show lower-tier performance, with PassMark database operations ranking in the bottom 10%.

The instance offers a cost-efficient entry point for compute-bound workloads that require dedicated CPU resources but do not demand large memory footprints or local storage. Due to the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and weak multi-core scaling, it is best suited for single-threaded applications, lightweight web serving, basic text processing, or utility scripting. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases, parallelized compilation, or high-throughput web applications.
